There have been 3,360 confirmed cases of the virus in the east of the country. Photograph: Dieudonne Dirole/EPA Global development Ebola outbreak in DRC the fastest growing in the history of the virus As the death toll rises to almost 1,500, and with a vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain potentially still months away, health workers face a battle to slow the outbreak Supported by About this content Prosper Heri Ngorora in Bunia Fri 31 Jul 2026 04.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 04.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The latest numbers of confirmed cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has made this latest outbreak the fastest growing in the known history of the virus. At 3,360 confirmed cases , the disease is now affecting people in five provinces in the east of the DRC, with 1,487 deaths recorded, representing an overall case fatality rate estimated at about 45%, according to Congolese health officials. Health responses to the outbreak have been badly hampered by conflict in many of the affected areas. “I fear that at some point, life may come to a standstill here in our province of Ituri,” said Deborah Nzuva, a mother of four who lives in Rwampara, one of the affected regions. “We were already in a precarious situation before the Ebola virus disease, which continues to claim its victims.” Since officially declared by the Congolese authorities on 15 May, the Bundibugyo strain of the virus has spread faster than any of the country’s 16 previous Ebola outbreaks – and the numbers are approaching the previous worst toll, in 2018-2020 when 3,470 people in DRC were infected. Prof Pierre Akilimali, from the country’s public health institute (NPHI), is in charge of the Ebola response. He emphasises that the disease continues to spread and that it is still difficult to know when it will reach its peak. According to him, there is a way to go and the road to bringing the outbreak under control is a long one. View image in fullscreen Members of a Congolese Red Cross team in Bunia carry the body of a woman suspected of having died from Ebola, 7 June. Photograph: Jospin Mwisha/AFP/Getty Images “Here in Ituri, we have the issues of insecurity, mining and high population density, which make the current outbreak more complex than previous ones,” he said. The Congolese authorities say they have taken a number of measures to limit spread, including strengthening surveillance through community liaison officers, building more than 20 Ebola treatment centres, and setting up local laboratories for testing. “The public must also play their part by seeking medical advice at the slightest suspicion of infection,” Akilimali said. “This will help us to respond effectively to the disease.” He said cases continue to rise in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones, with between 100 and 150 new confirmed infections each week. Annabelle Nissi, a clothing trader in Bunia, said people were living in fear. “This outbreak is causing us great distress. Our hope lies solely in God’s hands. It continues to disrupt our lives and has brought our development projects to a standstill,” she said. Dr Justus Nsio, field incident manager for the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, said it was a race against time. First patients enrolled in record-breaking Ebola treatment trial in DRC Read more “All the experts monitoring this outbreak agree that it was detected too late. When detection is delayed, we have to work hard to make up for what we missed earlier in order to contain the disease,” he said. “What is certain is that, with the commitment of the movement and our partners, the outcome will be favourable.” View image in fullscreen Health workers prepare for a safe burial operation in the community of Mongbwalu, Ituri, DRC, in May. Photograph: Michel Lunanga/Getty Images Clinical trials began in early July of a vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no standard treatment. As of 15 July, about 20 people had been enrolled in these trials, which could last up to four months, according to Prof Placide Mbala, head of laboratory operations for the Ebola response in the DRC. Uganda, which this week declared the Ebola outbreak over on its territory, 12 days after its last case was reported, has sent experts to the DRC to work alongside their Congolese counterparts, particularly in the border regions of Tchomia and Kasenyi. Saxony's State Criminal Police Office said the search for a second unidentified object would resume on Thursday morning. The explosive-laden drone was found overnight Tuesday into Wednesday on the airport's southern runway, according to investigators. Security sources said it was lying near a Ukrainian Antonov An-124 Condor transport aircraft. Federal police specialists later defused the explosive device. Investigators are also looking into a suspected second flying object that may have struck a cargo aircraft after it aborted its landing because of the runway closure. Beállítom Nem sokkal indítás után felrobbant a Kínai Népköztársaság egyik Hosszú Menetelés 7A hordozórakétája hétfőn délután – írja a South China Morning Post . A 60 méter hosszú, eddig kifejezetten sikeres rakétát a Vencsang Űrközpontból indították volna útnak, rakománya egy telekommunikációs műhold volt, amit a kínai űrügynökség geostacionárius pályára szándékozott állítani. Mind a rakétával, mind a műholddal elvesztették a kapcsolatot 90 másodperccel a kilövés után, a törmelék valószínűleg a Dél-Kínai-tengerbe zuhant. A ChinaSat-4B műhold ráadásul a Kínában eddig épített legdrágább műholdtípusba tartozik, egy ilyen műhold nagyjából 1 milliárd jüant, azaz majd 47 milliárd forintot ér. Hogy pontosan mi történt, azt egyelőre nem tudni, a kínai állami hírügynökség három órával az eset után annyit közölt, hogy „repülési anomália” áll a baleset hátterében. Szemtanúk szerint az úgynevezett Max Q pont környékén megroppanhatott a rakéta felső része. A Max Q azt a pontot jelöli, amikor egy kilövés után a legnagyobb dinamikus nyomás nehezedik a rakétára. A Hosszú Menetelés 7A modellnek eddig csak egyetlen sikertelen repülése volt, 2020 márciusában. A hibát akkor a négy gyorsítórakétában fellépő nyomásvesztés okozta, ami a vártnál alacsonyabb sebességhez és repülési magassághoz vezetett, végül pedig a küldetés megszakítását eredményezte röviddel a második fokozat működésének megkezdése után – írja a Spacejunkie .
